To obtain cash to refund the bills maturing October 17, 1960, and to provide the funds for the anticipated cash requirements of the Treasury during the remainder of the calendar year, an offering of two issues of Treasury bills was announced on October 6. The offerings consisted of: $1-1/2 billion of one-year (364-day) Treasury bills, dated October 17, 1960, to mature October 16, 1961, for cash or in exchange for the $2 billion of 320-day bills maturing October 17, 1960. 3-1/2 billion, or thereabouts, for cash of 244-day Treasury bills, tax anticipation series, dated October 21, 1960, to mature June 22, 1961. The amount included $500 million to cover the reduction in the October 17, 1960, bills. These bills will be acceptable at par in payment of income and profits taxes due June 15, 1961. Payment for accepted tenders for the one-year bills was required to be completed on October 17, 1960, in cash or other immediately available funds on in a like face amount of Treasury bills maturing on that date. Cash adjustments were made for differences between the par value of maturing bills accepted in exchange and the issue price of the new bills. For the 244-day bills, any commercial bank qualified as a depositary was permitted to make payment for the bills allotted to itself and its customers by credit in its Treasury tax and loan account up to the amount for which it was qualified in excess of existing deposits. Other subscribers to this issue were required to complete payment for accepted tenders at the prices offered in cash or other immediately available funds on October 21,1960. Tenders for both issues were received without deposit from incorporated banks and trust companies and from responsible and recognized dealers in investment securities. python3 << 'EOF'
import math

# Discount rates for 26-week Treasury bills
# September 1, 1960 and September 8, 1960
rate_sept1 = 2.825  # percent
rate_sept8 = 2.801  # percent

# Convert to decimal
r1 = rate_sept1 / 100
r2 = rate_sept8 / 100

# Compute weekly log return (as a return)
log_return = math.log(r2 / r1)
print(f"Rate Sept 1 (decimal): {r1}")
print(f"Rate Sept 8 (decimal): {r2}")
print(f"Log return: {log_return}")

# Compute squared return (realized variance for single period)
squared_return = log_return ** 2
print(f"Squared return (realized variance): {squared_return}")

# Annualize - for weekly frequency, multiply by 52
realized_variance_annualized = squared_return * 52
print(f"Annualized realized variance: {realized_variance_annualized}")

# Volatility is sqrt of annualized variance
volatility = math.sqrt(realized_variance_annualized)
print(f"Annualized realized volatility (decimal): {volatility}")

# Convert to percentage
volatility_pct = volatility * 100
print(f"Annualized realized volatility (percent): {volatility_pct}")

# Round to nearest hundredths
print(f"Rounded to hundredths: {round(volatility_pct, 2)}")
EOF
